children: Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - November 25, 2026) - IC Group Holdings Inc.

("IC Group" or the "Company"), a consumer engagement company driving commerce and data for global brands and professional sports teams, is pleased to announce its unaudited financial results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026. All figures are reported in Canadian dollars unless otherwise stated.

"Q3 2026 was our third consecutive quarter of Adjusted EBITDA at $0.67 million, up 64% from the prior year, on revenue growth of 11% that was approximately 98% organic," said Duncan McCready, CEO of IC Group. "IC Engage expanded its gross margin to 74% and IC Insurance grew revenue by 34%. IC Mobile grew revenue by 15%, but its gross margin remains below where it needs to be while we absorb carrier cost increases and operate two messaging platforms in parallel. We expect to complete the messaging platform migration in the fourth quarter. Together with the leadership realignment we implemented in October, that positions us to enter 2027 with a lower cost base and a clear path to margin expansion."
Select Q3 2026 Highlights
Revenue
for the third quarter of 2026 was $8.1 million, up 11% from $7.3 million in the same period of 2025. Approximately 98% of quarterly revenue growth was organic.
Annual Recurring Revenue ("ARR")
represented approximately 66% of total revenue in the third quarter of 2026, consistent with 66% in the same period of 2025.
Gross Profit
increased 4% to $3.4 million, compared to $3.3 million in the same period of 2025.
Gross Margin

was 42%, compared to 45% in the same period of 2025. The decrease was driven primarily by margin compression in the IC Mobile segment, where pass-through carrier costs increased faster than revenue and the Company incurred duplicate messaging platform costs, partially offset by margin expansion in IC Engage.
Net loss
improved to $0.14 million, compared to a net loss of $0.36 million in the same period of 2025.
EBITDA
increased 103% to $0.48 million, compared to $0.24 million in the same period of 2025.
Adjusted EBITDA
increased 64% to $0.67 million, compared to $0.41 million in the same period of 2025, and was consistent with the first and second quarters of 2026.
Year-to-date revenue
increased 21% to $24.0 million, while year-to-date Adjusted EBITDA increased 172% to $2.01 million.
Bank indebtedness
was reduced to $6.6 million at September 30, 2026, from $7.7 million at December 31, 2025, through scheduled principal repayments of $1.17 million. Cash was $2.3 million at September 30, 2026.
Q3 2026 Segment Highlights:
IC Engage
Revenue
increased 2% year-over-year to $3.4 million, against a strong comparative quarter that included a Fortune 50 technology client's program launches in new countries.
Gross Profit
increased 16% to $2.5 million, while Gross Margin expanded to 74% from 65%, reflecting lower direct labour and fulfillment costs and improved utilization of technology personnel.
Operating income
increased 36% to $0.74 million, compared to $0.54 million in the same period of 2025.

During the quarter and as previously announced, the Company entered into an exclusive three-year partnership with a leading global venue technology provider and signed a renewal and expansion agreement with a longstanding Fortune 50 technology client covering 30 countries. Refer to the news releases dated July 23, 2026, and July 8, 2026, respectively. At September 30, 2026, the Fannex platform was used by 101 teams, up from 94 a year earlier.
IC Mobile
Revenue

increased 15% year-over-year to $3.7 million, all of which was organic, driven by higher messaging volumes, particularly from wholesale customers, and carrier rate increases passed through to customers.
Gross Margin

was 8%, compared to 20% in the same period of 2025, reflecting a higher mix of wholesale traffic, industry-wide carrier price increases not fully recovered in customer pricing during the quarter, and higher platform-related costs during the migration.
Operating loss

was $0.37 million, compared to $0.15 million in the same period of 2025, due to the lower gross margin described above. Excluding $0.11 million of platform enhancement costs, the adjusted operating loss was $0.26 million.

As previously announced on July 16, 2026, the Company entered into a strategic relationship with Bullet Messaging Inc., including a five-year software-as-a-service agreement that gives IC Mobile exclusive Canadian licensing rights to Bullet's message routing platform. The Company expects to complete its transition to the enhanced messaging platform in the fourth quarter of 2026.
IC Insurance
Revenue

increased 34% year-over-year to $0.97 million, supported by new business under expanded underwriting authority, newly added brokers and the Players Health acquisition. Approximately 95% of the segment's revenue growth was organic.
Gross Profit

increased 22% to $0.57 million, while Gross Margin was 59% compared to 65% in the prior-year period due to higher brokerage commissions on increased premium volume and a lower commission rate on the new authority.
The segment generated operating income of $0.10 million, compared to $0.06 million in the same period of 2025.
Customers outside North America represented 19% of segment revenue for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to 9% in the same period of 2025.
Subsequent to Quarter-End

In October 2026, the Company implemented a leadership realignment to simplify its organizational structure and improve efficiency. The Company's Chief Operating Officer departed and other non-officer positions were eliminated. The Company expects to record a restructuring charge of approximately $1.0 million in the fourth quarter of 2026, consisting primarily of severance and related employee transition costs to be paid over approximately 14 months, and estimates annual savings of approximately $0.9 million from the eliminated positions. The charge is not reflected in the third quarter results.

Non-IFRS Measures

There are measures included in this news release that do not have a standardized meaning under International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) and therefore may not be comparable to similarly titled measures and metrics presented by other publicly traded companies. The Company includes these measures because it believes certain investors use them as a means of assessing financial performance. Adjusted EBITDA and Annual Recurring Revenue ("ARR") are financial measures that do not have standardized meanings under IFRS. Adjusted EBITDA refers to earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, amortization, stock-based compensation, one-time transaction expenses and financing costs. ARR refers to the Company's expected yearly revenue from recurring transactional, service, license, SaaS or subscription fees.

We prepare and release quarterly unaudited and annual audited financial statements in accordance with IFRS. We also disclose and discuss certain non-IFRS financial information used to evaluate our performance in this and other earnings releases and investor conference calls as a complement to results provided in accordance with IFRS. We believe that current shareholders and potential investors in the Company use non-IFRS financial measures, such as Adjusted EBITDA and ARR, in making investment decisions about the Company and measuring its operational results.

Management believes that investors and financial analysts measure our business on the same basis, and we are providing Adjusted EBITDA and ARR as financial metrics to assist in this evaluation and to provide a higher level of transparency into how we measure our own business.
Adjusted EBITDA is more fully defined and discussed, and a reconciliation to IFRS financial measures is provided, in the Management's Discussion and Analysis ("MD&A").
